items.q: What should you remember about **Two temperatures always**?
items.a: **shell (skin) and core (viscera/CNS) are** distinct; brain integrates shell signals to drive heat dump or behavioral exit.

items.q: What should you remember about **POA is the hub**?
items.a: **preoptic area over roof** of mouth; controls autonomic sweating/vasodilation and amygdala-linked "get out" agitation.

items.q: What should you remember about **Sitting sauna ≈ cardio**?
items.a: **HR 100–150, plasma volume ↑,** stroke volume ↑; not a substitute for loaded exercise/bone density.

items.q: What should you remember about **Frequency dose-response**?
items.a: **more sauna sessions/week →** greater cardiovascular and all-cause mortality reduction (confounders controlled).

items.q: What should you remember about **GH requires infrequent shock**?
items.a: **heat adaptation blunts GH spike; once/week or** every 10 days for maximal release; 4×30 min same day is the study protocol.

items.q: What should you remember about **Discomfort is the mood feature**?
items.a: **dynorphin from safe-but-uncomfortable heat** primes endorphin system efficiency over time.

items.q: What should you remember about **Evening heat, evening cool**?
items.a: **post-sauna cooling parallels sleep-onset temperature** drop; cold before bed can raise core temp and impair sleep.
